title: Deployment Cadet Checklist & Rollout Architect Notebook (Sept 2026) - Draft
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational notebook for an upcoming rollout. Combine checklist hygiene with a lightweight calendar and a short release notes draft so on-call and product owners can run a 48h watch without digging through three separate docs. Meant to be lightweight and editable in-flight.

Scope:
- Target: hosted API model routing changes + canary config for smart-routing fallback (no schema change)
- Surface area: serving runtime routing layer, traffic split service, telemetry exporters, console flags
- Excludes: model weight changes, infra maintenance windows (separate ticket)

Standing assumptions / constraints:
- Quiet window: 09/20 00:00 - 09/26 06:00 PT (minimal planned ops) but we have a 72h watch after rollout
- Primary region: us-west1; secondary fallback: eu-west1
- SLA tier impacts: none expected for <5% traffic shifting; plan includes throttles at 1%, 5%, 15%, 50%

Week-at-a-glance (calendar):
- Mon 09/13: Final preflight dry-run (dev cluster); smoke tests green -> tag canary-rc. Tasks: QA signoff, perf bench (90th latency check)
- Tue 09/14: Ops rehearsal; on-call pairing walkthrough; update playbook snippets
- Wed 09/15: Release notes draft posted to #release-ops; stakeholder sync 11:00 PT (PM, SRE, Eng)
- Thu 09/16: Telemetry baseline collection (last 7 days) and acceptance thresholds locked
- Fri 09/17: Freeze config; commit canary policy; schedule rollout window
- Mon 09/20: Launch day - execute micro-canary -> observe -> expand across lanes

Preflight checklist (must be GREEN before we tag and schedule):
- [ ] Code/Config review: all PRs merged and tagged (PR redwood/serving-runtime#4128 merged)
- [ ] Smoke tests: end-to-end smoke suite passing on dev and staging (attach run ids)
- [ ] Load sanity: perf bench showing <=+8% 95th latency vs baseline for target seq_len 512
- [ ] Telemetry: dashboards created and templated; data retention for watch window in place
- [ ] Alerts: temporary tuned alerts created (rate/latency/error rate) and routed to #release-watch
- [ ] Fallback routes: variant model pinned and validated for automated fallback
- [ ] Ops runbook: one-page playbook available in Slack pinned thread + printed checklist in ops binder
- [ ] Stakeholder notify: customer success & GTM heads notified (email + slack thread)
- [ ] Rollback package: documented rollback commands and PR to revert config change ready

Micro-canary execution plan (day-of steps):
- Step 0: Ensure all participants online; on-call ack in #release-watch; double-check runbooks
- Step 1: Route 1% traffic to canary for 15 minutes (observe)
- Step 2: If no block, move to 5% for 30 minutes and run targeted synthetic prompts (lists below)
- Step 3: 15% for 1 hour (heat-check automated metrics + manual quick QA)
- Step 4: 50% for 2 hours with staggered regional ramps (us-west -> us-east / eu fallback)
- Step 5: Full ramp beyond 50% only if both automated gates and human sign-off are clear

Gating criteria (automated checks that MUST pass to move to next step):
- Error rate: increase <= 0.5 percentage points over baseline (1m rolling)
- 95th latency: <= baseline + 20% absolute (sequence length specific)
- Token generation quality: basic hallucination regression check (eval set) shows no >3% delta in correctness score
- System resource: GPU utilization < 85% sustained; no sudden OOM events in logs

Telemetry & dashboards to monitor (short-list):
- Route-level RPS / 1m / 5m
- Error counts by type (503, 429, model-timeouts)
- P50/P95/P99 latency for generation endpoint by seq_len bucket
- Token-level cost per 1k tokens (estimate) so finance knows impact of ramp
- KV cache hit-rate for streaming requests
- Synthetic eval runner: results and diff visualization (attach screenshot in Slack)

Alert tuning (temporary):
- Alert A: route_error_rate > baseline + 0.5% for 10m -> P1 to on-call
- Alert B: P95 latency > baseline + 25% for 15m -> P1 to on-call + page ENG-SRE
- Alert C: token budget > projected * 2 in 1h -> notify finance and product ops

Rollback matrix (quick reference):
- Symptom: spike in 5xxs across routes -> Action: rollback routing config to previous canary (runbook id: RB-091)
- Symptom: sustained P95 > threshold -> Action: scale down traffic to 0% for affected region and open immediate incident
- Symptom: QA eval regression > 3% -> Action: immediate rollback and hold deployment; begin triage with model/quality team

Communication plan (who says what):
- Pre-launch (T-48h): Mail to stakeholders (pm@, cs@, legal@ if needed) with link to playbook and expected watch hours
- During launch: #release-watch pinned updates every step completion + short human note (ops lead)
- Major blocks/incidents: Page ENG-SRE and AC tream; designate comm lead to draft internal incident note
- Post-completion: Release summary to #release-ops + weekly digest to execs

Release notes (short draft to publish post-success):
- Title: Routing Policy Update & Canary Strategy for Smart-Routing (Sept 2026)
- Summary: We’re rolling out a new routing policy that enables smarter fallback behavior for latency-sensitive routes. The rollout will be gradual (1% -> 50%) with telemetry-driven gates to ensure no regression in latency or error rates.
- Impact: No API contract changes. Expected minor fluctuation in cost while caching warms. No customer action required.
- Rollback: Revert to previous routing config and pin model variant (instructions for engs included in ops runbook).
- Owners: Aisha Patel (Release Lead), Marco Ruiz (SRE), Jing Wu (Quality)

Post-release checklist (within 48h):
- [ ] Confirm long-tail P99/P99.9 behaviors over 24h window
- [ ] Validate billing delta and notify finance if >5% beyond projection
- [ ] Rotate off temporary alert rules after 48h (or keep if useful)
- [ ] Capture watch notes and convert to a short postmortem if any non-trivial anomaly observed
- [ ] Merge any hotfixes to main and tag a stable release

Field notes / miscellaneous (notes to self):
- Keep synthetic eval set short: ~15 prompts representing worst-case tokens and medium tokens. Make sure prompt seeds include function-calls path.
- Remind QA to run both streaming and non-streaming paths; streaming often masks KV cold starts.
- If we see a cost spike with stable latency, check cache-key collisions and prefix caching behavior.
- Consider adding an extra telemetry dimension: average per-request KV cache entries.

Open questions / action items (unresolved):
- Who signs off on final rollout beyond 50%? (PM and SRE lead recommended)
- Do we need legal or CS escalation for enterprise customers if we see latency regressions in their tenants?
- Confirm whether dedicated customers on Dedicated clusters are impacted or excluded by org-level routing policy (action: @Marco to confirm with platform).

Quick links & references (to paste in thread):
- Runbook template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/runbook-template
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4128
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RE-2331
- Slack convo: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02RELEASEOPS/p1632456000

Appendix: quick copyable commands (ops):
- Rollback routing config: curl -X POST https://internal-api/route/revert -d '{"tag":"previous"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
- Pin model variant: cli-tool model pin --env=prod --route=smart-routing --variant=stable-v3
- Check telemetry snapshot: ./tools/telemetry-snapshot --route smart-routing --window=15m > /tmp/snap.txt

End notes: keep this doc as the single source for the 48h watch — update it in-line with major observations, mark each step with time and initials. This is intentionally terse; expand into full postmortem only if anomalies appear.
